newsitem.title: FRANCE: French employer sued for non-smoker's cancer death.
newsitem.headline: French employer sued for non-smoker's cancer death.

text.p: Lawyers acting for the family of a non-smoker who died of lung cancer urged a Paris court on Wednesday to condemn the dead woman's employer for failing to impose French laws limiting smoking at work.

In a case unprecedented in France, the sister of Lebanese-born Leila Ozeir and two anti-smoking associations are seeking 50,000 francs ($10,000) damages from Ozeir's employer, the Banque Francaise de l'Orient.

Luc Bihl, lawyer for Ozeir's sister, argued in court that Ozeir's fatal cancer was caused by inhaling her colleagues' cigarette smoke after the bank failed to implement tough 1991 laws restricting smoking at work. Ozeir died in 1995, aged 44.
The Paris court said after Wednesday's hearing that it would deliver a ruling on November 20.
